title: Environmental Conventions and Biodiversity Hotspots: Quiz

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is concerned with the conservation of:
questions.rationale: Ramsar (1971) protects wetlands of international importance. Migratory species fall under the Bonn Convention (CMS).

questions.question: Which treaty regulates international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora?
questions.rationale: CITES, adopted in Washington in 1973, controls trade. CMS conserves migratory species themselves, and Basel deals with hazardous waste.

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol (1987) aims to:
options: Cut greenhouse gas emissions of developed countries
questions.rationale: Montreal phases out CFCs and similar chemicals. The binding emission cuts belong to the Kyoto Protocol (1997).

questions.question: The Basel Convention deals with:
questions.rationale: Basel (1989) controls hazardous waste crossing borders. POPs are Stockholm (2001) and prior informed consent is Rotterdam (1998).

questions.question: Which pair of treaty and year is correctly matched?
questions.rationale: Minamata, on mercury, was adopted in 2013. Kyoto was adopted in 1997 and entered into force in 2005; Stockholm is 2001; Cartagena is 2000.

questions.question: The Kigali Amendment (2016) relates to which treaty and which group of chemicals?
questions.rationale: Kigali amends the Montreal Protocol to cut hydrofluorocarbons, which warm the climate though they do not deplete ozone.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots that include Indian territory?
questions.rationale: Succulent Karoo is in southern Africa. India's parts are in the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland.

questions.question: The Nicobar Islands form India's part of which biodiversity hotspot?
questions.rationale: The Nicobar Islands are the Indian portion of Sundaland. Indo-Burma covers north-eastern India.

questions.question: A biodiversity hotspot must have lost at least what share of its original vegetation, and have at least how many endemic vascular plant species?
questions.rationale: The two criteria are 1,500 endemic vascular plants and at least 70 percent habitat loss. The concept came from Norman Myers in 1988.

questions.question: Which statement about Indian Ramsar and conservation facts is correct?
options: Chilika and Wular are on the Montreux Record
Keoladeo and Loktak are on the Montreux Record
questions.rationale: Only Keoladeo and Loktak appear on India's Montreux Record. UNEP is at Nairobi, Ramsar at Gland, and India joined in 1982.

questions.question: Arrange the IUCN categories from more to less threatened. Which of these is the correct ordering of three?
questions.rationale: The ladder runs Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, then Near Threatened and Least Concern.

questions.question: The Paris Agreement was adopted at which Conference of the Parties?
questions.rationale: Paris (2015) was COP21. Kyoto came from COP3 in 1997 and India's net-zero 2070 pledge was announced at COP26.

questions.question: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in which year, and after which event?
questions.rationale: The Act of 1986 followed the Bhopal gas leak of 1984. The Rio Summit was in 1992, and the Wildlife Protection Act is the 1972 law.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct date and observance?
questions.rationale: 5 June is World Environment Day. 22 May is the Day for Biological Diversity, 2 February is Wetlands Day and 16 September is Ozone Day.

questions.question: The Cartagena Protocol, an agreement under the Convention on Biological Diversity, is about:
questions.rationale: Cartagena (2000) covers biosafety. Access and benefit sharing is the Nagoya Protocol of 2010, the usual distractor.
